newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar extends rally but backs off high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar extends rally but backs off high.

text.p: London white sugar futures burst higher on Monday in an extension of the morning's rally after stops were triggered in New York but then ran into a bout of profit-taking at the highs.
Earlier in the session a mixed bag of broker, commission and trade buyers pushed August to a high of $315.10, nearly $2.00 up on Friday's close.
But then the raws market opened and July broke through buy stops at 10.92 and 11.00 cents/lb, reaching a high of 11.08
But July baulking at the key point of 11.10 sparked some quick profit-taking in London, where the spot August contract hit its head on $317.00 resistance.
"August reacted to a high of $317.00 which is quite important...both books are holding well so we will possibly see a test of the upside towards the close," said one trader.

One leading commission house was said to have been an active buyer during afternoon activity. August/October continued to widen in flat-price dealings but traders said activity was more concentrated in December/March.
At 1540 GMT August was up $2.70 at $316.00 and October up $2.50 at $305.50. Market volume reached a solid 1,915 lots, dominated by August trades.
"August is very popular all of a sudden and seems to have many friends -- they're expecting a shortage of sugar," said another trader.
August is a time of seasonal tightness as sugar from the European Union's new crop has yet to appear on the market and traders have to rely on the tail-end of the current crop for their supplies.
The Paris market was quiet by comparison with just 86 lots traded. August was up $2.70 at $316.00 and October was untraded.
